title: Investigate and Fix Reserved-Pool Autoscaler Failing to Provision Burst Capacity
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Multiple Dedicated customers experienced degraded throughput when requests that should have triggered burst provisioning were served by overloaded nodes instead. Symptoms: elevated request latencies, queueing at the front-end, and rapid token drain on reserved pools. Initial triage indicated the autoscaler reconciler did not create new burst allocation pods for some pools under sustained short-term load spikes.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create a dedicated reserved pool with reserved_capacity=100 GPUs and burst_limit=40
2) Send a sudden burst of requests that would require additional 30 GPU equivalents for ~90s (simulate client ramp)
3) Observe autoscaler logs: expected: allocation of ephemeral burst nodes; observed: reconciler logs a no-op and metrics show burst_tokens decreased without node creation
4) Recreate in staging using the load generator script at https://git.redwood.ai/dedicated/loadgen/tree/burst-scenarios (branch: reproduce/autoscaler-8172)
immediate_mitigations: 1) Manually scale up affected reserved pools via console to restore capacity for impacted customers
2) Temporarily increase burst_limit for critical tenants as a stopgap (requires manual oversight)
3) Added short-term alert to PagerDuty escalation (#pager-duty-dedicated) for any pool where queued_requests > 0 for > 20s
4) Rolled out a hotfix to the request-router to prioritize prefix caching hits to reduce cold-start pressure
root_cause_summary: A race condition in the Dedicated autoscaler reconciler combined with incorrect accounting of burst tokens caused the controller to early-exit without provisioning ephemeral capacity. Two factors contributed: (a) the pool token accounting path decremented available tokens when evaluating prospective allocations (pre-commit) leading to negative effective capacity under concurrent reconcile attempts; (b) the node-provisioning client call was not retried on transient quota-check 429s due to missing idempotency keys — so provisioning requests were dropped silently in a subset of regions.
proposed_fix: 1) Move token decrement to post-success commit (atomic commit path) so tokens are only consumed after provisioning is confirmed
2) Add CAS (compare-and-swap) semantics on token state using the existing pool-lock with optimistic backoff
3) Add idempotency keys to node-provisioning requests and implement exponential retry on 429/5xx for up to 30s
4) Improve telemetry: emit provision_attempt_{start|success|failure} and pool_snapshot metrics so we can correlate decisions with observed capacity
5) Add unit tests that simulate concurrent reconciles and an integration test in the e2e harness that simulates quota throttling
rollout_plan: 2) Deploy to 10% of Dedicated clusters (canary tag) for 24 hours with close monitoring
3) If canary is green (no repro of queued_requests > 0 and provision_success_rate > 98%), expand to 50% for 12 hours
4) Full rollout to all Dedicated regions if metrics stable; if any region degrades, rollback specific region and investigate
5) Post-rollout: keep enhanced PagerDuty alert for 7 days then evaluate alert fatigue
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: provision_success_rate < 95% over 5m for any pool -> P0 escalation
Alert: queued_requests > 10 for > 30s for any reserved pool -> notify on-call and auto-open ENG ticket
